Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
5th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● Commercial vessel traffic through Strait of Hormuz has increased since signing of the now-collapsed US-Iran MoU. Only 731 transits were recorded between the signing and July 29, compared to a pre-conflict average of around 138.

● Houthis of Yemen said they will attack Saudi oil tankers in the northern Red Sea off the Yanbu area after vessels re-routed to avoid the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

● One person was killed and 11 wounded in an Israeli strike on Tebnine, southern Lebanon. The area is separate from where the IDF issued an evacuation notice earlier.

● Iranian and Omani negotiators finalized a draft deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, now awaiting final sign-off from Iran's supreme leader.

● UKMTO reported an incident 95NM southeast of Aden, Yemen. A loud explosion in close proximity to the vessel was heard. All crew were safe, and there was no environmental impact.

● The US Treasury Dept officially lifted counterterrorism sanctions from two aircraft and three airlines tied to IRGC.

END OF THE BRIEF

Netram Defence Review (@NetramDefence)

Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
4th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● Saudi Aramco is routing crude around the Strait of Hormuz via its East-West pipeline as the Iran-related crisis has cut shipping through the strait to a tenth of pre-conflict levels.

● Qatar’s PM and FM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani called on all parties to implement the US-Iran MoU, including its provision on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, during a phone call with Russian FM Sergey Lavrov.

● Iraq exported more than 30 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz between July 4 and Aug 4, down ~71% from its pre-war monthly average of 105 million barrels.

● Indian cargo vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya capsized and sank after being hit by a projectile near Yemeni waters. All seafarers were rescued by the Yemeni Coast Guard.

● As of today, CENTCOM has redirected 45 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two as part of the naval blockade on Iran.

END OF THE BRIEF

tweets.title: Iran Seeks Greater Control Over Strait of Hormuz An Iranian official says Tehran is negotiating exclusively with Oman on a temporary 1–3 month arrangement that would give Iran primary control over security and maritime services in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran insists it is not negotiating the status of the strait with the United States, and says several issues must be resolved before broader progress is possible, including: - Implementation of previous commitments - Sanctions relief - Release of frozen Iranian assets - The situation in Lebanon Iranian officials also said the temporary shipping corridor under discussion with Oman would remain in place until a permanent arrangement is agreed.
tweets.content:
Iran Seeks Greater Control Over Strait of Hormuz

An Iranian official says Tehran is negotiating exclusively with Oman on a temporary 1–3 month arrangement that would give Iran primary control over security and maritime services in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran insists it is not negotiating the status of the strait with the United States, and says several issues must be resolved before broader progress is possible, including:

- Implementation of previous commitments

- Sanctions relief

- Release of frozen Iranian assets

- The situation in Lebanon

Iranian officials also said the temporary shipping corridor under discussion with Oman would remain in place until a permanent arrangement is agreed.
